data: In slot filling performance, is the performance of the Spanish model better than the performance of the Thai model, when using 100% of the training data?

The question asks whether the performance of the Spanish model is better than the performance of the Thai model when using 100% of the training data. From the caption, we know that the dashed line represents the performance of the Attention-Informed Mixed Training (Att.) model with 100% training data, and the solid line represents the performance of the proposed model by varying the proportion of training data size. 

Looking at the graphs:

- For slot filling (subfigures (a) and (c)):
  - The orange line (Spanish) is consistently above the blue line (Thai) across all β values.
  
- For intent detection (subfigures (b) and (d)):
  - The orange line (Spanish) is also consistently above the blue line (Thai) across all subset sizes.

Therefore, based on the visual evidence, the performance of the Spanish model is better than the performance of the Thai model when using 100% of the training data.
